title: Bluetooth setting shows misleading message when systemd service for it is disabled
line: When the Bluetooth service isn't running, the Bluetooth settings page and applet now say so instead of "No devices paired" or offering to enable Bluetooth.
explanation: The KCM only had placeholders for no adapters (rfkill state Unknown) and for Bluetooth turned off (shown only while BluezQt's Manager is operational). With bluetoothd not running the manager is not operational, so neither matched and the KCM fell through to "No devices paired", while the applet showed "Bluetooth is disabled" with an Enable button that only unblocks rfkill. Both now check Manager.operational and show "The Bluetooth service is not running" with no action; the KCM adds a short explanation.

commits.message:
kcm, applet: say when the Bluetooth service is not running

When bluetoothd was not running, the KCM said "No devices paired" and
the applet offered to enable Bluetooth, though neither could help. Both
now say that the Bluetooth service is not running, with no action.

BUG: 481513

review.text: Checking BluezQt.Manager.operational in both the KCM and applet fixes the misleading 'No devices paired' / 'Bluetooth is disabled' placeholders when bluetoothd is stopped, while keeping 'No Bluetooth adapters' higher priority. However, in src/kcm/ui/main.qml the header's 'Enabled' switch (toggleBluetoothAction) stays visible and interactive because it only checks rfkill state, even though its checked state tracks bluetoothOperational and clicking it cannot start bluetoothd (it visually flips the switch on while the page still says the service is not running). Hiding toggleBluetoothAction when !BluezQt.Manager.operational matches the applet toolbar and the commit message's 'no action' behavior.
changes: In src/kcm/ui/main.qml, gate toggleBluetoothAction.visible on BluezQt.Manager.operational as well (visible: BluezQt.Manager.operational && BluezQt.Manager.rfkill.state !== BluezQt.Rfkill.Unknown) so the KCM header does not show a broken 'Enabled' switch when the Bluetooth service is not running.
Retake after-1.png and update the notes/verify description after hiding the KCM Enabled toggle when bluetoothd is stopped.

reviews.text: Right diagnosis and layer: with bluetoothd down BluezQt.Manager.operational is false, so the KCM fell through to 'No devices paired' and the applet offered an rfkill Enable that cannot help. The new placeholders and the excluded applet action are correct, and the real-bluetoothd regression check is good. But the KCM still shows its 'Enabled' switch (visible whenever rfkill state isn't Unknown, as after-1.png shows), right above a message saying Bluetooth cannot be used. Flipping it only unblocks rfkill and powers adapters, the same futile action the reporter complains about and that this patch already removes from the applet.
changes: In src/kcm/ui/main.qml hide toggleBluetoothAction when the service is not running, e.g. visible: BluezQt.Manager.operational && BluezQt.Manager.rfkill.state !== BluezQt.Rfkill.Unknown, and re-check after-1.png.
